decision_questions_inherited_from_TASK_1: Q1: Where does the registry live - artifacts/scripts/ paired or artifacts/governance/ unpaired?
Q2: Does the registry use a single file or per-domain split?
Q3: Is RACI_MATRIX (legacy) deprecated outright in favor of RACI_MATRIX_V2 in the registry, or do both ship?
Q4: Does extraction precede or follow the validator module split?
Q5: How is schema validation enforced - in-runner at startup, or via a separate quality-gate?
Q6: Do registry changes require waiver/decision artifacts (governance change) or are they treated as ordinary code changes?
Q7: How is RACI_MATRIX_V2 frozenset preserved through JSON round-trip (since JSON only has arrays)?
Q8: What is the rollback plan if registry-driven runtime regresses?

migration_options.title: do_not_extract_in_v3_5_1
pros: consistent with v3.5.1 plan §9.2 default defer
cons: does not leverage TASK-1031 candidate listing
validator split v3.6 prerequisite (policy boundary clarity) unresolved
RR-5 RACI v1/v2 drift risk lingers
risks: if v3.6 split starts without extraction design, split-time policy double-write becomes risk source
migration_options.recommended_followup: re-evaluate before v3.6 implementation start; do not jump to implementation

migration_options.title: extract_before_validator_split
pros: cleaner module boundaries during split (policy externalized)
exposes schema validation / migration risks earlier
cons: extraction itself complex (high-risk slices include EXACT_SYNC_FILES self-ref / RACI v1/v2 unification)
8 design questions must be solved first; single design task insufficient capacity
baseline / EXACT_SYNC_FILES expansion needs separate task first
risks: if extraction introduces regression (e.g., frozenset round-trip type loss), split is further deferred
extraction rollback path not yet defined
preconditions: all 8 design questions closed via narrower design tasks
schema prototype validated under PCACC strict scope
rollback plan formalized (sha256 restoration / runner re-baseline)
migration_options.recommended_followup: execute Option D (schema prototype) first; then re-evaluate B

migration_options.title: extract_after_validator_split
pros: post-split each new module's policy boundary naturally narrower; extraction can proceed per-module
cons: split-time policy double-write complexity = (split + extract) compounded
split blocked by RC-7 (decomposition strategy) unsatisfied; extract chained behind
multi-module baseline expansion = multiple governance changes; high churn
risks: during split, policy without extraction may be copy-pasted across new modules; introduces silent divergence (RR-5 same family)
preconditions: validator split done + verify pass + green at least one release cycle (v3.5 plan §5.6 / version_split_rule)

migration_options.title: schema_prototype_design_first_implementation_later
pros: lowest-risk forward path; designs schema and contract only; no runner / validator / template change
provides shared contract for narrower follow-up tasks (Option E step 1)
cons: does not directly reduce split-time risk; still needs implementation task
risks: if schema prototype chooses wrong (e.g., single file vs per-domain split), downstream follow-ups must rework
preconditions: TASK-1031 readiness gate documentation referenceable (already done)
Q1 (registry location) + Q2 (single vs per-domain) + Q5 (schema validation enforcement) have provisional answers
migration_options.recommended_followup: draft contract for Q1/Q2/Q5 via narrower design task; then decide whether to enter Option B

migration_options.title: split_design_into_smaller_followups
pros: directly addresses TASK-1031's 8 design question multi-axis complexity
preserves dedicated design space for Q3 (RACI unification) / Q7 (frozenset round-trip) / Q8 (rollback)
composes with Option D (first narrower design task = schema prototype)
cons: multiple design task closure conditions need extra design
risks: without shared schema prototype, narrower design tasks may drift; mitigation: list schema prototype as the first prerequisite
preconditions: TASK-1032 done + verify pass (will be satisfied at this commit)
migration_options.recommended_followup: schema prototype -> low-risk slice extraction design -> medium-risk slice extraction design -> high-risk slice + RACI unification

limitations: TASK-1032 is design-decision only; this artifact records option evaluation, not implementation contracts.
Recommendation `split_design_into_smaller_followups` defers contract details to narrower design tasks; this artifact does not create those tasks.
Candidate registry slice IDs (RC-A..RC-I) are organizational heuristics; final partitioning is determined by narrower design tasks.
Risk register (DR-1..DR-6) covers design-level risks; runtime risks of any future extraction are out of scope.
Readiness gates RG-1..RG-10 reference TASK-1031 RC IDs and design-level prerequisites; satisfaction is required before v3.6 extraction implementation, not before this decision.
Schema validation requirements (§6 of design artifact) are written as forward-looking constraints for future extraction; this artifact does not define a concrete JSON Schema.
Source/template sync implications inherit QC-SYNC-001 semantics proven by TASK-1029; no new sync gate logic is proposed.
Backward compatibility concerns BC-1..BC-5 reflect current v3.5.0/v3.5.1 contracts; future contract evolution requires separate decisions.
The 8 inherited design questions are listed as inputs; this artifact intentionally does not give per-question contracts (that work is the scope of narrower design tasks).
Follow-up candidate task IDs (TASK-1033..TASK-1038) are advisory; actual ID allocation is governed by future v3.6 task allocation lifecycle and may differ.
